newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe wants "realistic" euro-dollar rate post - EMU.
newsitem.headline: Juppe wants "realistic" euro-dollar rate post - EMU.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday the planned euro currency must have a "realistic" parity against the dollar, based on fundamentals.

Juppe, speaking in a radio interview five days ahead of parliamentary elections, said a realistic dollar exchange rate was one condition for the euro to become an "instrument for growth" after the launch of European monetary union in 1999.
"...there should be a realistic parity between the euro and the dollar which reflects the economic reality and not some kind of theoretical target," Juppe told RTL radio.
He did not mention any figures.

Juppe said another condition for growth under the euro was political oversight over growth targets and major economic decisions which ought not to be left solely in the hands of the European central bank.

He said this had been built in to the plans for a so-called stability council of ministers from euro-zone countries, which had been given a wider mandate for growth as well as budgetary rigour on France's insistence.
Juppe dismissed four conditions for EMU laid down by opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin, saying they might be designed to endanger the project.

Jospin's conditions include avoiding overvaluation of the euro against the dollar, bringing Italy and Spain in to the single currency from the start and creating a new pact for growth and solidarity to promote jobs.
"We have made conditions so that the euro will succeed. I rather have the feeling that Mr Jospin is making conditions so it will fail," Juppe said.
